user.title: Before you start
user.description: Foyer is offered as software that automates actions on rules, not as an alarm system. It is not certified (EN 50131, CEI 79-3), not monitored, not a fire alarm, and comes with no warranty and no promise of support (Apache-2.0, sections 7 and 8). Do not rely on it alone to protect people or property: keep certified smoke alarms, and a professional installation where a policy or a risk calls for one.

init.title: Recover access to Foyer
init.description:
For an administrator who holds no code in a house where others do, or whose own Foyer user was disabled. The account's Foyer user is enabled, its validity window removed and its code replaced; an account with none gets a new user with every permission.

**This is never quiet.** It is written in the log, shown as a Home Assistant notification and sent to every contact, naming the account. If you did not mean to do this, close the window.

data_description.account: Only administrators' accounts are listed: Home Assistant does not tell Foyer who opened this window, so choose yours. Anybody else is given a way in from the Users page.
data_description.code: Exactly {length} digits, not already somebody else's.

zone_unreachable.title: Foyer: {zone} has not been seen for {days} days

confirm.title: Mark as seen
confirm.description:
The zone {zone} has been unreadable for {days} days. While it is, it is a fault: it blocks arming and it is never treated as “closed”. A flat battery, a sensor out of range, or an integration that no longer loads.

Confirming closes this notice. It comes back if the problem returns.

channel_broken.title: Foyer: {service} is not there to call

confirm.title: Mark as seen
confirm.description:
The notification channel {service}, which {contact} is reached through, is not in this Home Assistant any more. Integrations get removed, renamed or fail to load after an update, and a channel discovered broken during an alarm is the failure this check exists to prevent. Fix it on the Contacts page and send a test.

Confirming closes this notice. It comes back if the problem returns.

confirm.title: Mark as seen
confirm.description:
Messages to {contact} through {service} have failed repeatedly. The service is there; the sends are not arriving. Send a test from the Contacts page once you believe it is fixed — a success clears this.

Confirming closes this notice. It comes back if the problem returns.

watchdog_never_worked.title: Foyer: the external watchdog has never answered

confirm.title: Mark as seen
confirm.description:
Not one ping has succeeded since it was switched on. Almost always a mistyped URL or an endpoint that was never created. Foyer does not show the saved URL, so there is nothing to check it against: type it again on the System health page. Last error: {error}. Until it works, nothing outside the house knows whether Home Assistant is still alive.

Confirming closes this notice. It comes back if the problem returns.

watchdog_unreachable.title: Foyer: the external watchdog has stopped answering

confirm.title: Mark as seen
confirm.description:
The pings are failing. Last error: {error}. Being unable to reach it means no notification that needs the internet would reach you either.

Confirming closes this notice. It comes back if the problem returns.

confirm.title: Mark as seen
confirm.description:
{count} of {of} zones on {radio} went quiet at once while the coordinator kept answering. This is a heuristic, not jamming detection: a coordinator crash, a firmware update, a channel change or a power cut to a room of mains-powered routers all look exactly like this.

Confirming closes this notice. It comes back if the problem returns.

coordinator_down.title: Foyer: the coordinator of {radio} is unreachable

confirm.title: Mark as seen
confirm.description:
{entity_id} cannot be read, so no zone on {radio} is being watched. This is not interference — it is the coordinator, its power or its network. A coordinator on Power-over-Ethernet dies with its switch.

Confirming closes this notice. It comes back if the problem returns.

mains_lost.title: Foyer: the house is running without mains power

confirm.title: Mark as seen
confirm.description:
{entity_id} reports that mains power has failed. Everything that needs the internet stops when the router does.

Confirming closes this notice. It comes back if the problem returns.

confirm.description:
Foyer is offered as software that automates actions on rules, not as an alarm system. It is not certified (EN 50131, CEI 79-3), not monitored, not a fire alarm, and comes with no warranty and no promise of support (Apache-2.0, sections 7 and 8). Do not rely on it alone to protect people or property: keep certified smoke alarms, and a professional installation where a policy or a risk calls for one.

The alarm keeps working until you do.
